## Overview of [TradingView](https://in.tradingview.com/?aff_id=167054)  
TradingView is a web‑based charting platform that has become a favorite among retail traders, analysts, and even some institutional users. Its biggest draw is the clean, modern interface that works in any browser, plus a powerful scripting language called Pine Script for building custom indicators and strategies. The social side is also strong—users can publish ideas, follow other traders, and comment on charts in real time. Because it lives in the cloud, you can access your saved layouts from any device without installing software.

## Overview of Thinkorswim  
Thinkorswim (often shortened to TOS) is the desktop‑centric trading suite offered by TD Ameritrade (now part of Charles Schwab). It provides a full‑featured environment for equities, options, futures, and forex, with deep analytical tools, advanced order types, and a robust paper trading mode. Thinkorswim’s strength lies in its desktop power—complex studies, thinkScript coding, and a highly customizable workspace that many professional traders rely on. While it does have a web version, the desktop client remains the primary way most users interact with the platform.

## Feature Comparison  
When you line up TradingView vs Thinkorswim, several categories stand out.

### Charting Tools  
Both platforms excel at charting, but they approach it differently. TradingView offers over 100 built‑in studies, drag‑and‑drop drawing tools, and a library of community‑created scripts that you can instantly add to any chart. Thinkorswim matches that with hundreds of studies, plus the ability to layer multiple charts in a single window and use the “thinkScript” editor for sophisticated studies. If you love sharing ideas publicly, TradingView’s social charting feels more natural; if you need deep backtesting and complex option analytics, Thinkorswim often edges ahead.

### Scripting and Automation  
Pine Script (TradingView) is relatively easy to learn, making it ideal for traders who want to prototype indicators quickly. ThinkScript (Thinkorswim) is more verbose but offers greater control over order logic, making it better suited for automated strategies that interact directly with brokerage accounts. Both languages have active forums, yet Thinkorswim’s integration with live trading can be a deciding factor for algorithmic traders.

### Market Data and Broker Integration  
TradingView provides real‑time data for many exchanges through paid data plans, but it does not execute trades itself—you must connect a broker via its broker integration feature. Thinkorswim, being a brokerage platform, streams live data directly from TD Ameritrade/Schwab accounts and lets you place trades without leaving the app. This all‑in‑one approach can reduce latency and simplify workflow for those already with Schwab.

### Mobile Experience  
TradingView’s mobile apps are highly rated for their responsiveness and feature parity with the web version. Thinkorswim’s mobile app exists, but many traders find it less intuitive for charting, preferring the desktop for serious analysis and using the phone mainly for watchlists and alerts.

## Pricing and Plans  
Cost is often a deciding factor.

### TradingView Pricing  
TradingView offers a free tier with limited indicators and one chart per layout. Paid plans start at around $14.95/month (Pro), $29.95/month (Pro+), and $49.95/month (Premium), each adding more indicators, multiple charts per layout, and priority customer support. Data fees are extra if you need real‑time exchange data beyond the basic free feeds.

### Thinkorswim Pricing  
Thinkorswim is free to use if you have a funded TD Ameritrade/Schwab account; there are no platform fees. You only pay standard commissions and fees for trades, plus any market data subscriptions you opt for (e.g., NYSE, NASDAQ, or international data). For traders who already maintain a brokerage account with Schwab, the platform cost is effectively zero.

## Ease of Use  
TradingView’s interface feels modern and lightweight, making it easy for newcomers to jump in and start charting within minutes. Thinkorswim has a steeper learning curve due to its depth—menus, tabs, and countless settings can overwhelm beginners, but power users appreciate the granular control. If you value a plug‑and‑play experience, TradingView wins; if you enjoy tinkering with every setting, Thinkorswim rewards the effort.

## Community and Support  
TradingView shines with its social network: you can publish trading ideas, follow other analysts, and engage in comment threads directly on charts. This community aspect can be a great source of inspiration and learning. Thinkorswim offers solid support through TD Ameritrade’s customer service, extensive educational webinars
